citation.title: Components of sensorimotor adaptation in young and elderly subjects

study.eligibility_rationale: Upper-extremity visuomotor rotation with young vs old adults, reporting both the adaptation phase and the no-feedback after-effect phase: "Twelve young and twelve old subjects executed center-out pointing movements while visual feedback about their fingertip was either veridical (baseline), 60-deg rotated (adaptation), or absent (after-effect)." Written in English.
study.design_notes: Single experimental sample (12 young, 12 old) performed, in sequence: baseline pointing, 15 adaptation episodes with +60° rotated feedback, 5 after-effect episodes without feedback, 3 'refresh' episodes with rotation re-instated after a 5-min break, and 10 transfer episodes of TRACKING under rotation. Only the first adaptation block and its immediately following no-feedback after-effect phase are used; the refresh phase is a repeated exposure ("three refresh episodes of pointing with feedback again rotated by +60°") and the tracking transfer involves a contextual change of movement category (pointing → tracking), so both are dropped per dataset rules 2 and 3. A SEPARATE control sample ("additional twelve young (22.6±1.9 years of age) and twelve old (72.5±6.0 years of age)") never performed the pointing task and did tracking only, with no after-effect (no-feedback) phase; text says they did "five tracking episodes with +60° rotated feedback" whereas Fig. 2 appears to plot thin control lines across episodes 11–20 — a possible text/figure discrepancy. Group ns are identical in Methods and results (F(1,22) for the pointing ANOVAs implies 24 analysed subjects); the transfer ANOVA reports F(1,43), implying 47 rather than 48 subjects in that analysis, a discrepancy the paper does not explain. No numeric group means/SDs for adaptation or after-effect are printed in the text; they appear only in Fig. 1.

datasets.chosen_pair_rationale: The experimental young (26.0±5.0 y) and older (69.5±7.5 y) groups are the only pair that performed the pointing adaptation and the no-feedback after-effect phase. The tracking-only control groups (young 22.6 y, old 72.5 y) were not exposed to the pointing perturbation and have no after-effect phase, and the pooled 54-senior sample has no young counterpart.

outcomes.measure_name: Angular pointing error (median initial movement direction error per episode)
outcomes.higher_is_better_evidence: Their errors increased abruptly at the onset of the adaptation phase, and then gradually dropped again. Most importantly, adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects.
outcomes.operationalization: Angular error of the initial direction of pointing responses (median across responses per 50-s episode, per subject) during the 15 adaptation episodes with +60° rotated visual feedback (Fig. 1 episodes 6–20). Late adaptation = the last adaptation episode (episode 20, filled symbols, immediately before feedback removal); an alternative operationalization is the asymptote of the exponential fit to the adaptation time course reported in the text.

datasets.notes: Outcome values are shown only graphically: "Fig. 1 Mean pointing errors of young (triangles) and old (squares) subjects before, during, and after exposure to rotated visual feedback... Also shown are the standard deviations". Dependent variable is the median initial direction error (angular error, deg); smaller error = better adaptation during the adaptation phase, whereas the after-effect deviation magnitude indexes recalibration. Reported statistics: adaptation Age F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05; after-effect ANOVA gave no significant Age effect (only Episode F(4,88)=66.84 and interaction F(4,88)=3.95).

study.notes: The PDF contains only the two figures detected; there are no data tables, so all numeric outcome values must come from Fig. 1 (means and SDs plotted per episode) plus the ANOVA statistics in the Results text. Text-reported numbers are limited to trail-making times (young 27.4±7.2 s, old 42.5±6.9 s), normalized trail-making scores, and the pooled-senior adaptation magnitude (0.49±0.21), none of which are protocol outcomes. Tracking-only control groups were not entered as a dataset because their exposure is a different task with no aftereffect phase and their values appear only in Fig. 2.
